observation_summary: 30k source vs 18k target points; density_ratio 0.77 (target slightly sparser), bbox ratio 0.88, centroid offset 0.595 (~17.6x base_scale, large initial misalignment relative to object scale). Rotation magnitude and overlap are NOT_IMPLEMENTED, so true initial pose error is unknown but likely beyond ICP's convergence basin.

candidate_methods.pros: Cheap and fast; excellent convergence when initial pose is already close and overlap is clean.
candidate_methods.risks: Centroid offset is ~17.6x base_scale with unknown rotation; identity initialization will very likely converge to a poor local minimum or fail on valid correspondence.

candidate_methods.pros: SOR + FPFH + RANSAC provides a pose estimate that is robust to large rotation/translation offsets; SOR handles the small outlier fraction indicated by the NN statistics; point-to-plane ICP refines.
candidate_methods.risks: Slower; FPFH matching quality depends on feature distinctiveness; a too-tight global correspondence threshold risks zero RANSAC inliers, so the threshold must be generous.

reasoning_summary: Large centroid offset relative to base_scale with unknown rotation makes identity-initialized LOCAL_ICP high-risk. Choose the global pipeline first. global_corr_scale=6.0 gives a RANSAC correspondence distance of ~0.204 (generous, covers the expected initial misalignment while staying inside the 2.0-10.0 guardrail range); icp_max_corr_scale=1.5 (~0.051) is slightly above the source spacing to keep ICP on valid inliers after RANSAC initialization.
